evidence_items.publisher: Endor Labs, distributed by PR Newswire
evidence_items.explanation: The April 15 published benchmark snapshot reports 84.4% functional correctness and 7.8% security correctness for Cursor with Claude Opus 4.6. These paired results support a substantial gap; the event date denotes the reported snapshot, not the dates individual benchmark runs were executed.

This earlier study examines repeated extensions of agent-generated code and reports deterioration in structural quality. It broadens the context beyond security, but its March findings are not treated as an April outcome.

The study reports weak self-detection of correctness and safety problems, but also substantial ability to repair flawed code when supplied with test or analysis feedback. That favorable finding limits any stronger interpretation that LLM systems cannot help improve robustness.

unresolved_gaps: The decisive April snapshot comes from a security vendor and is not an independently replicated estimate of all production code.
The benchmark does not comprehensively measure architectural quality, maintainability, or reliability.
The evidence does not isolate next-token prediction as the cause of the gap.
